Category: Vehicle.

spec.name: Spitfire Blueprint
spec.description: A Supermarine Spitfire Mk I fighter, built as a cyanotype blueprint: Prussian-blue surfaces in three tones, with chalk-white panel lines, ribs, rivet rows and dashed centre lines on every part.
spec.layout:
Single-engine low-wing monoplane in a level attitude, nose toward +Z, thrust line on y = 1.7 and x = 0. Spinner tip z = +4.6, rudder trailing edge z = -4.6, wingtips x = ±5.6, fin top y = 2.95. Left is +X, and every pair is mirrored with s = ±1. Only the two main wheels (y = 0) and the tail wheel (y = 0) touch the floor.

FUSELAGE STATIONS (z: centre y, half-width, half-height), with an elliptical cross-section:
3.5: 1.70, .38, .38 (cowl lip)
3.0: 1.70, .43, .42
2.2: 1.70, .45, .47
1.4: 1.72, .44, .52
0.4: 1.68, .42, .52
-0.8: 1.62, .38, .50
-2.0: 1.55, .30, .40
-3.0: 1.50, .17, .28
-3.7: 1.45, .08, .20 (tailRoot)
The tail cone then tapers to a rounded tip at z = -4.35, y = 1.40.
The long cowled nose is lower than the cockpit deck. The bubble-less sliding canopy peaks at y = 2.62 near z = -0.2, with a three-pane windscreen at z ≈ 1.2 and a fairing behind it that blends into the spine by z = -1.6.

WING (elliptical, thin, with 6° dihedral). Stations (x: LE z, TE z, centre y, thickness):
0.45: 1.25, -1.35, 1.15, .32
1.5: 1.20, -1.30, 1.26, .28
3.0: .95, -1.15, 1.42, .20
4.5: .45, -.95, 1.58, .13
5.3: -.05, -.75, 1.66, .09
The tip is rounded at x = 5.6, y = 1.70, z ≈ -0.4. The wing root is buried in the fuselage from x = ±0.3. Ailerons run x 3.2 to 5.1 (rear ~28% of chord), and split flaps run x 0.7 to 2.6.

TAILPLANE (elliptical, tapered): y = 1.47, tips x = ±1.65, root LE z = -3.3, TE z = -4.2, tip LE -3.85, TE -4.1. The elevators are the rear 35% (hinge z ≈ -3.88 at the root).
FIN (elliptical): LE rises from (z -3.35, y 1.7) to the top at (z -4.15, y 2.95). The rudder hinge is z ≈ -4.1 to -4.15. The rudder is broad and rounded, with its TE bulging to z = -4.6 near y 2.2.

GEAR (down): short legs from the wing underside, a little splayed outward, with tyre radius 0.36 and width 0.16, wheel centres at y = 0.36. The tail wheel has radius 0.12, on a strut about 1.2 m long.

PROPELLER: 3 broad scimitar blades, radius 1.5 from the hub. Blade directions (clock angle from up): 180° (straight down, tip y = 0.2), 60° and 300°. The blades turn on the propeller joint, and the spinner is an ogive from z = 3.5 (radius 0.34) to 4.6.

BLUEPRINT STYLE ON EVERY PART: all surfaces are flat blues, and there are no reds, yellows or greens. Colour follows place: up-facing skins use skinTop, flanks use skinBase, and undersides and recesses use skinShade or skinDeep. Hard edges are chalk-white `line` strips about 4 mm wide and 3 mm proud, on leading edges, control-surface outlines, canopy frames and cowl seams. Panel lines, wing ribs and spars are thinner `lineSoft` strips. Rivet rows are tiny lineSoft spheres or discs. `lineFaint` marks secondary construction lines, such as dashed centre lines along the spine, the wing span axis and the fin. Roundels are concentric discs seated on the skin, outer to inner: line, skinDeep, lineSoft, accent-blue centre. Everything is faceted low-poly with bold readable shapes.

parts.builds:
Everything of the airframe body from the cowl lip (z = 3.5) back to tailRoot (z = -3.7). It is a loft through the fuselage stations in the layout, in skinBase with skinTop on the upper deck and skinShade on the belly.
- Nose: cowl panel seams in line, three cowl-fastener rivet rows in lineSoft, a chin carburettor intake under the nose (z 2.2 to 3.2, skinDeep mouth with a lineSoft lip), and a small oil-breather bump.
- Exhaust: six short ejector stacks per side at z 2.0 to 3.0, y ≈ 1.78, x ≈ ±0.43, in metalDark with skinDeep openings.
- Gun troughs: faint gun-bay panel lines.
- Cockpit: a sill, a windscreen of three glass panes with a line frame, a sliding canopy in glass with line framing ribs and a glassDark rim, a head-armour fairing behind it, a reflector gunsight (accentCyan glow glass) at the windscreen base, and a small entry flap with handle on the left side.
- Aerial mast at z ≈ 1.9, y 2.12 to 2.55, in metal.
- Markings: a fuselage roundel (line, skinDeep, lineSoft, roundelCore rings, radius ≈ 0.38) on each flank at z ≈ -2.4, y ≈ 1.58, and code letters and a serial drawn as small line-coloured parts or an svg decal on the flanks.
- Lines: a dashed lineFaint centre line along the top spine, rivet rows along the flanks, and a white line along the wing-root join.
The wing and gear attach to it, and it does not build the wing root fillets.
parts.attaches: Front face at noseBase meets the propeller part's spinner back plate. Rear face at tailRoot meets the tail part's cone. The wing root buries into the belly at wingRootL and wingRootR. Rides joint fuselage.

parts.builds:
Both elliptical wings as lofts through the wing stations, with dihedral, in skinTop above, skinShade below, and a white `line` leading-edge strip.
- Surfaces: rib lines (lineSoft thin strips) every ~0.35 m across the upper surface, spar lines, and a dashed lineFaint span axis.
- Roots: wing-root fillets blending into the fuselage.
- Control surfaces: ailerons (x 3.2 to 5.1, riding aileronL and aileronR) with fabric-rib stripes and outline in line, and split flaps inboard (x 0.7 to 2.6) with skinDeep hinge gaps.
- Guns: four .303 gun ports per wing in the leading edge, with short metalDark barrel stubs poking forward and a skinDeep ejection chute slot underneath.
- Cooling: an oil-cooler scoop under the left wing and a glycol radiator scoop under the right wing at x ≈ ±2.4 (box-like fairings with skinDeep mouths, metal grilles and line rims). A landing light lens in the left leading edge, and a pitot tube on the left underwing.
- Gear: wheel-well outlines in skinDeep under the wings near the gear mounts.
- Markings: a roundel on each upper wing at x ≈ ±3.7 and one on each lower wing (outer line ring, skinDeep ring, lineSoft ring, roundelCore centre, radius ≈ 0.5), in sunk-in flat discs seated on the skin.
- Tips: rounded wingtips with a small navigation light in accentCyan.
- Rivets: rivet rows in lineSoft along the spar and root.
parts.attaches: Roots start at wingRootL and wingRootR and bury 0.12 m into the fuselage. Ailerons ride aileronL and aileronR at the aileronHinge mounts. The main legs attach to the underside at gearAttachL and gearAttachR. The rest rides joint fuselage.

parts.builds:
The tail cone from tailRoot to tailTip (a tapering loft in skinBase with a skinShade belly and a rounded end) and all the empennage.
- Fin: an elliptical fin extruded in skinBase with a skinTop edge, carrying a broad rounded rudder on the rudder joint. The rudder has horizontal rib stripes in lineSoft, a trim tab, a white hinge line and a white outline.
- Tailplane: two elliptical tailplanes at y ≈ 1.47, in skinTop above and skinShade below, with leading-edge line strips, rib lines and rivet rows.
- Elevators: one on each side, riding elevatorL and elevatorR, with rib stripes, a small trim tab on the left and a line outline.
- Markings: a fin flash on each side of the fin, made of three stacked vertical stripes (line, skinDeep, roundelCore), a small rear navigation light in accentCyan at the rudder base, and a dashed lineFaint centre line on the fin.
The tail wheel and its strut belong to the gear part.
parts.attaches: The cone starts at tailRoot, flush with the fuselage rear face, and ends at tailTip. The stabs start at stabRootL and stabRootR, and the elevators hinge at elevatorHingeL and elevatorHingeR. The fin sits on the spine at finBase and ends at finTop, and the rudder hinges at rudderHinge. The tail wheel strut hangs from tailWheelMount, below the cone.

parts.builds:
The whole propeller assembly, on the propeller joint (axis +Z).
- Spinner: an ogive lathe from z = 3.5 (radius 0.34) to the tip at z = 4.6, in spinner with a lineSoft ring near the base, a thin line ring mid-way, and a faceted highlight stripe.
- Back plate: a skinDeep backplate disc at z = 3.5 to 3.56, with a ring of small metal bolts.
- Blades: three broad scimitar-shaped blades, radius 1.5 from the hub, twisted a little, at clock angles 180° (down), 60° and 300° from up. Each is skinBase with a skinTop leading edge, a lineSoft tip band, a white `line` leading-edge strip, and a tiny line serial stamp.
- Roots: a metalDark root cuff and a metal blade-root collar per blade.
The tip of the lowest blade clears the floor at y ≈ 0.2.
parts.attaches: The back plate sits flush on the fuselage front face at noseBase, centred on propHub. Spinner tip at spinnerTip.

parts.builds:
All the running gear.
- Main legs: two main legs in metal and metalDark, from gearAttachL and gearAttachR down to the wheel centres, splayed outward a little. Each has an oleo strut with a lineSoft scissor link and a brake line, plus a hinge pivot fairing at the wing.
- Wheels: two wheels riding wheelL and wheelR, each with a faceted tyre (tyre colour, radius 0.36, width 0.16), a metal hub disc, a skinDeep brake drum, a ring of bolts in lineSoft, a white `line` hubcap ring, and a few tread notches.
- Doors: an outer gear door hanging from each leg, in skinShade with a white outline and a skinDeep inner face.
- Tail wheel: a tail wheel riding tailWheel (radius 0.12, tyre colour, metal hub) on a tailStrut oleo from tailWheelMount, with a small fork.
The lowest points of the three wheels touch y = 0.
parts.attaches: The main legs top out on the wing underside at gearAttachL and gearAttachR. The wheel hubs are centred on wheelCenterL and wheelCenterR. The tail strut hangs from tailWheelMount (under the cone), and its wheel centre is tailWheelCenter.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching out a spec for a Spitfire in cyanotype blueprint style, weighing whether the model should be static or have joints for the propeller, control surfaces, and landing gear. I'm leaning toward keeping it modest, with a root fuselage, a propeller joint, and aileron hinges, and I'm starting to pin down the Mk I dimensions: an 11.23 m wingspan and a 9.12 m length.

I'm settling on a level-ish pose for the Spitfire, with the thrust line horizontal so the main and tail wheels sit on the floor, and I'm estimating the prop tip clears the ground at about 0.15 m. That puts the overall box at roughly 11.2 by 3.0 by 9.1 m, with the spinner and rudder trailing edge centred near z = ±4.55.

I'm now settling on the visual treatment: a cyanotype blueprint look with deep blue skin tones and white or pale cyan line work for panel lines, rivets, roundels, wing ribs, and the cockpit frame. I'm also sketching a palette of named blues and whites to keep the colours consistent across the parts.

I'm laying out the parts list now: the fuselage with its canopy, exhaust stacks, and roundels, then the wings with ailerons, flaps, and underwing radiators, the empennage with fin, rudder, and tailwheel, and I'm starting on the propeller and nose section.

I'm now placing the propeller and nose: the spinner and three blades will sit forward of the fuselage front at about z=3.5, with the prop box spanning z 3.4 to 4.6 and a radius of 1.6 centred on y=1.75.

I'm checking the overall height now, since a 3.35 m figure would overshoot the 3.0 m estimate, and the fin top sits lower than the propeller. I'm settling on a thrust line at 1.7 m with a 1.55 m prop radius, which puts the blade tips about 0.15 m off the floor and the top near 3.25 m. I'm working out how the three blades should sit at rest so the lowest one still clears the ground.

I'm checking the blade angles now: one blade pointing straight down with the other two at 60 degrees either side of vertical. That keeps the lowest tip about 0.15 m off the floor and the top of the assembly near 2.95 m, so the 3.0 m height estimate still holds. I'm also starting to sketch the landing gear part, with the main legs, wheels, doors and fairings, and I'm wondering whether the tailwheel belongs there too.

I'm deciding on the rest of the parts list: the wheels, hubs, gear doors and wheel wells, plus the tailwheel, with the gear legs hinged. I'm also weighing the propeller part, which is looking thin, so I'll give it the spinner, the blades and their roots, the backplate, and the chin intake under the nose.

I'm sizing the wing next: the root chord sits near 2.6 m where it meets the fuselage at x ≈ ±0.45, tapering to a rounded tip of about 0.9 m at x ≈ ±5.6.

I'm working out the wing's placement: root leading edge at z=1.25 and trailing edge at z=-1.35, a 2.6 m chord, sitting around y=1.0 with a slight dihedral. I'm checking whether the tips rise to about 1.5, and whether the main gear legs from x=±1.9 down to the wheels still clear the wing underside at about y=0.95.

I'm working out the main landing gear positions now: the legs attach to the wing underside around x=±1.25, and the wheels sit a bit further in, near x=±1.0, since the Spitfire's track is fairly narrow. I'm weighing whether the legs should splay outward, and I'm checking that the wheel centres stay about 0.35 m off the floor.

I'm working out the main gear positions now: the legs hinge from the wing underside near x=±0.95 and angle only slightly outward, with the wheels at about x=±1.05 and a 0.38 m radius so they just touch the floor. I'm checking that the wing root thickness of roughly 0.3 m still leaves room for that attachment, and placing the wing centre around y=1.15.

I'm checking the wing's centreline height against the thrust line, so the tip sits roughly level with the propeller axis. I'm also setting the fuselage centreline at 1.7 m at the nose, with a fairly deep body, and I'm wondering whether its underside sits below the wing.

I'm settling the fuselage profile now: the root depth sits around 1.1 m, with the canopy rising about half a metre above the deck. I'm keeping the rear fuselage fairly straight and leaving the tail centreline a little below the nose.

I'm checking the tail assembly now: the fin base sits behind the tailplane, with its top near y 2.95, and I'm placing the rudder hinge around z -4.15. I'm also weighing how the tailwheel fits, since at this level pose it would need a long strut to reach the floor.

I'm weighing whether the rear fuselage should droop so the tailwheel reaches the floor without a 1.4 m strut. A simpler route than tilting the whole model is to let only the rear keel curve down, with the spine line running from the nose toward the tail.

I'm now fixing the tailwheel mount just behind the tail, with the spine running as a smooth curve from the nose to the tail end so the fuselage and tail agree. The strut would be about 0.9 m long, which I'll accept as plausible for a Spitfire-style oleo.

I'm defining the fuselage centreline along the spine, from the nose down to the tail root, and assigning each point a half-width and half-height so the body tapers from the cowl back to the tail.

I'm adjusting the fuselage's vertical profile, settling the half-heights along the body so the top deck and bottom line come out around 2.1 m and 1.1 m near the centre.

I'm settling the fuselage spine points now: the nose sits at about y 1.7, with the cockpit section rising slightly higher, and the body tapering down toward the tail. I'm also setting the canopy top at about y 2.6.

I'm now writing out the joint layout: the fuselage root sits on the spine with a propeller hinge at the nose, and the aileron hinges go on the wings, with the left aileron spanning roughly x 3.3 to 5.0.

I'm now fixing the wing planform as a station table: at the root the leading edge sits near z=1.25 and the trailing edge near z=-1.35, with the centre height around y=1.15 and a thickness of about 0.32, and I'm roughing in how these values shift further out toward the tip.

I'm working out the wing's planform as a station table, with the leading and trailing edges, centre height, and thickness set at each spanwise point. I'm also checking the chord at the outer stations and the wing's height at the gear attachment.

I'm fixing the wing's attachment point at about x=0.95 with the wheel centred near x=1.05 on a 0.38 m radius, and I'm checking that the underside clears the gear top. I'm also estimating the radiator scoops under the wings at x=±2.5, where the underside sits near 1.3 m, so a 0.3 m box would still sit clear of the floor.

I'm placing the aileron hinges now, with each one running along the trailing edge at roughly x 3.2 to 5.1, since the aileron takes up the rear 28% of the chord. The hinge sits near z -1.12 at the inboard end and around -0.8 at the outboard end, so the line follows the wing's trailing edge.

Now I'm working out the aileron hinges and the elevator and rudder joints for the tail, checking the fin base and the rudder hinge height. I'm also comparing the total length against the spinner tip and tail extremes, which comes out to roughly 9.2 m.

I'm sizing the overall box at roughly 11.2 by 3.0 by 9.2 m, with the spinner tip and rudder trailing edge both reaching about z = ±4.6. The fuselage tail end stops around z = -4.3. I'm also laying out the tailplane, with its root leading edge near z = -3.25 and a tapered span of about ±1.65 m, and placing the elevator and rudder hinges at their joints.

I'm finishing the fin and rudder placement, with the rudder hinged around z -4.1 and running back to the trailing edge near -4.6. I'm also setting the tailwheel mount just behind the tail and working out the wheel's small radius, then I'll turn to the propeller and gear joints.

I'm listing the joints now: the propeller and the aileron and elevator hinges, the two main gear legs with their wheels, and the tail strut with its tailwheel, all hung from the fuselage. That makes thirteen joints in total.

I'm working through the joint ownership, assigning the wing parts to the fuselage and aileron joints, the tail to the elevators and rudder, the propeller to its own joint, and the gear to the legs, wheels, and tail strut. I'm also starting on the blueprint colour palette, beginning with a deep blue for the background.

Still working out the colour palette: I'm filling in a set of named blues for the body, shading, and cavities, with white chalk lines for outlines and panel detail, plus a pale blue for the canopy glass.

I'm settling the colour palette now, with a deep blue skin and a lighter blue for the top surfaces, shading for the undersides and cavities, and white chalk lines for outlines and panel detail. I'm also keeping the roundels in the same monochrome scheme, using the line, deep and soft-line tones for their rings and centre.

I'm now listing the colour palette itself: a deep blue skin, lighter top surfaces, darker shading for the undersides, white and pale-blue line work, and a few cyan and glass tones for the cockpit and instruments.

I'm now laying out the finishing details for the model: panel lines as thin raised strips, rivet rows, wing ribs on the upper surfaces, and a dashed white centreline along the fuselage spine. I'm also getting into the fuselage parts list, with its bounding box starting to take shape.

I'm working out the fuselage bounds now, with the body box spanning roughly x ±0.55 so the exhaust stacks fit inside. I'm checking that the chin intake's lowest point, around y 1.17, still stays above the floor line.

I'm working out the wing's bounding box now, from x ±5.6 out to the tips, with the z range running from the leading edge back past the trailing edge so the cannon barrels and radiators fit inside. The underside should drop to about 0.9 so the radiator scoops are covered.

I'm checking the tail bounds now: a box from about z -4.6 to -3.1 covering the fin, rudder, stabilisers and elevators, with the fuselage handling the body up to the tail root. The tailwheel stays with the gear.

Setting the tail part to end at z -3.2 so it overlaps the fuselage's rear section, where the fin attaches. The fuselage box runs back to z -3.7, which leaves the rear cone for the tail to cover.

I'm setting the propeller box to span about z 3.5 to 4.6 and y 0.2 to 2.5, since three blades at 60 degrees either side of vertical give a radius that reaches roughly 1.35 m sideways.

I'm now detailing the spinner and the three propeller blades, with the spinner's base radius and its taper toward the tip, and setting the blade roots and hub bolts. Next I'm budgeting the landing gear parts: legs, oleo scissors, wheels with hubs and tread, doors, and brake lines, plus the tailwheel.

I'm setting the landing gear box to cover the main legs and wheels, roughly x ±1.35, y 0 to 1.15, z -4.15 to 0.95, so the tailwheel gets folded into the same bounds. I'm also adding the outboard main gear doors hanging from each leg, and I'm turning to the wing's fabric ailerons and inboard flaps next.

I'm placing the Brownings and roundels next: four gun ports per wing, with the ejection chutes dark underneath, plus a pitot tube, a landing light on the left leading edge, and roundels on both wings and the fuselage.

I'm placing the aerial mast just ahead of the cockpit at about z 1.9, rising from y 2.12 to 2.55, and I'm also checking the windscreen, sliding hood and headrest fairing so the canopy frame lines stay consistent. I'm noting a thin wire running from the mast toward the fin tip as a possible detail.

I'm working out the exhaust stacks next, and I'm settling on six per side, with the cannon barrels and aerial left out of this pass.

I'm now placing the exhaust stacks and the chin intake under the nose, plus the oil cooler under the port wing. I'm also planning the cowl panel lines and rivet rows, the centreline dash, and the cockpit sill with the pilot seat and control column seen through the glass.

I'm writing down the mount points now, starting with the nose base at the front of the cowl and the thrust axis at the same height.

Now I'm listing the mount points: the nose base and thrust axis at the front, the cockpit centre, the wing roots and tips on each side, the aileron inner hinge, the gear attachments and wheel centres, and I'm starting on the tail root.

I'm placing the tail stabilisers at about y 1.47, with the roots near z -3.3 to -4.2 and tips reaching x ±1.65, then setting the fin base up from y 1.5 to a top near 2.95, with its leading edge starting at z -3.35.

I'm laying out the tail end of the fin and rudder profile, then the tailwheel mount, and now starting a shared fuselage spine table with centre heights and half-widths at each station, beginning at the cowl front.

Still working through the fuselage spine table, checking the half-widths and heights at each station from the nose back toward the tail.

I'm changing the wheel dimensions to a tyre radius of 0.36 m and a width of 0.16 m, with the wheel centres at y 0.36 and x ±1.05, so the lowest point sits right on the floor. I'm also starting to note the tailwheel's radius.

Still defining the joint list, starting with the fuselage root and the propeller hinge along the nose axis...

I'm listing the joint definitions for the elevators, the rudder, the main gear legs with their wheels, and the tail strut with its tailwheel, each anchored to its parent part and oriented along its hinge direction.

I'm settling the elevator hinges at the root of the tailplane, around z -3.88, with the tip hinge a little further back. The rudder hinge runs up the fin near z -4.1, and I'm working out where the fin's leading edge curves up toward its top.

I'm now budgeting the parts at roughly 810 units in total: fuselage 220, wings 240, tail 130, propeller 90, and landing gear 130. I'm also settling the layout conventions, with +X to the left, the model facing +Z, the wings mirrored and dihedralled, and the colours assigned by surface: top skin, side skin, and shaded undersides.

I'm now setting the shared constants and the joint and part conventions: the joints get created first, parts attach to them by name, and floor-contact is only for the landing gear, while the propeller's lowest blade tip is kept clear of the ground.

I'm finishing up the spec now, filling in the mount points and wrapping up the layout details.
